providers.name: Aether
providers.tagline: A Firecracker VM per coding-agent task, running your own Claude Code or Codex, billed in credits for active VM time.
providers.summary: Aether runs each coding-agent task in its own Firecracker microVM, an Ubuntu workspace with persistent storage, a terminal, a browser and SSH access. You bring Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode on your own subscription or API key (or buy model calls separately), and Aether bills the VM in credits for active runtime only, per second. Workspaces suspend when idle and resume where they left off. Plans grant monthly credits, and credit packs cost $0.10 per credit.
providers.isolation: Firecracker microVM per task, not reused across tasks or users
providers.regions: Not stated on the pages checked.

rates.instance: Medium: 2 vCPU / 8 GB / 20 GB volume (10 credits per hour at $0.10 per credit)
rates.billingIncrement: per second (credits prorated by the second)
rates.billedWhile: Only while the workspace VM is active. Idle and suspended workspaces are not billed; a workspace suspends once no task, background activity or interactive connection holds it.

plans.limits: 20 credits a month (about 2 hours of Medium, or about 4 hours of the Small size listed on the homepage), 1 warm slot, 3 tasks at once.

plans.name: Starter
plans.limits: 400 credits a month (about 40 hours of Medium), 2 warm slots, 10 tasks at once.

plans.name: Pro
plans.limits: 2,000 credits a month (about 200 hours of Medium), 3 warm slots, 25 tasks at once.

pricing.freeTier: Free plan: 20 credits a month at no cost, permanently (about 2 hours of the 2 vCPU / 8 GB Medium size).
notes: Pricing is in credits. We convert at the credit-pack price of $0.10 per credit (packs of 100 for $10 up to 1,000 for $100, never expire). Medium uses 10 credits per hour = $1.00/hour, Large (4 vCPU / 16 GB) 20 = $2.00/hour, XL (8 vCPU / 32 GB) 40 = $4.00/hour. Each size doubles the previous one.

Included plan credits are converted at the same $0.10 per credit: Free 20 = $2, Starter 400 = $40, Pro 2,000 = $200, Max 4,000 = $400. Bought through a plan, credits cost less: about $0.075 (Starter), $0.0375 (Pro) and $0.03 (Max) each.
There is no billing after the credits run out: task starts are refused until you buy a credit pack or the plan renews. Packs are prepaid top-ups available on every plan.

Conflict between vendor pages: the homepage says 1 credit = 12 minutes on a default Small devbox (1 vCPU, 4 GB), with Medium (2 vCPU, 8 GB) at 2x and Large (4 vCPU, 16 GB) at 4x. The docs list only Medium, Large and XL, say Medium is the default size, and price Medium at 10 credits per hour. The rates agree (Small would be 5 credits = $0.50 per hour); we show Medium because both pages list it.

On 'boat placements' a workspace is metered per resource instead: 1 credit per CPU-hour and 1 credit per GB-hour of memory while it works, nothing while idle (12 credits per hour for Medium at full use). The pages checked do not say when a workspace runs on a boat placement.
Memory is stated in GB; we treat it as GiB.
Mobile testing devices also spend credits: 1 credit a minute for an Android emulator or Gradle build sandbox, 2 for an iOS simulator or Xcode build sandbox.
Model calls through Aether's own inference are charged at provider list price to a separate prepaid balance, not to credits. Calls on your own subscription or key are not billed by Aether.

Lifetime: the homepage says a devbox and its volume are destroyed when the task's pull request merges or closes, or after 48 hours of inactivity. The docs describe suspend on idle and an option to keep a workspace active.

bestFor: Running Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode on your own subscription in a cloud VM you can watch, steer and SSH into.
Task-per-VM agent work tied to GitHub pull requests, Slack, Linear or schedules.
Bursty agent work, since idle and suspended workspaces cost nothing.

providers.name: Agent37 Cloud
providers.tagline: Persistent agent sandboxes billed per minute from a prepaid wallet, with optional full VMs and auto-sleep.
providers.summary: Agent37 Cloud runs persistent instances for code, services and agent harnesses, managed through a REST API with a Python client. Default instances are gVisor-isolated containers on shared hosts in the United States; VM instances (own kernel, KVM) cost 2.5x the compute rate and also run in France, the UK and India. Rates are published per 730-hour month ($0.80 per vCPU, $0.70 per GB of RAM, $0.09 per GB of disk) and metered per minute: compute while running, disk while the instance is kept. There is no subscription; usage draws down a prepaid balance.
providers.isolation: gVisor per default instance; optional VM instances with their own kernel and KVM hardware virtualization
providers.regions: Default instances run in the United States. VM instances run in us, eu (France or the UK) and ap-south (India, Mumbai); outside the US only VM instances are available.

rates.billingIncrement: per minute
rates.billedWhile: Compute (vCPU and RAM) for the whole time an instance is running, including starting and other transitional states. Sleeping or stopped instances bill disk only.

plans.name: Prepaid wallet
plans.limits: No subscription or minimum; top-ups of $5 to $10,000. The limit is the memory running at once: 32 GB before the first top-up, 40 GB after it, 200 GB once top-ups total $50, 800 GB at $250 and 3,200 GB at $1,000. Sleeping and stopped instances do not count. Max per instance: 4 vCPU and 32 GB RAM on default instances, 8 vCPU and 64 GB RAM on VM and Performance instances.

pricing.freeTier: One-time $5 starter credit after adding a card (the card is not charged), for new accounts; up to 3 instances running at once until the first top-up.
notes: Rates are published per 730-hour month: $0.80 per vCPU, $0.70 per GB of RAM and $0.09 per GB of disk. We divide the vCPU and RAM rates by 730 to get hourly figures; the disk figure is shown per month as published.

These are default-instance rates. VM instances bill compute at 2.5x and Performance instances (dedicated cores) at 4x; disk is unchanged. Default instances share host hardware, so sustained heavy CPU use may be limited when the host is busy.
RAM is stated in GB without saying GB or GiB; we treat GB as GiB.

Shapes are fixed: 2 vCPU / 4 GB, 4 / 8, 4 / 16 and 4 / 32 on every type, and VM and Performance instances also offer 8 vCPU / 64 GB. A default instance that asks for more than 4 vCPU is provisioned at 4 vCPU. The 64 GB shape is larger than the memory an account can run at once before its top-ups total $50 (32 GB, then 40 GB).

Auto-sleep is off by default; when on, an instance sleeps after an idle timeout (default 900 seconds, from 5 minutes to a day) and wakes on the next request. In-memory state usually survives a wake but is not guaranteed. Instances parked in cold storage bill $0.03 per GB-month on compressed bytes stored.
Creating an instance requires one day of its running rate in the wallet. Managed models, search and integrations are billed separately from the same wallet.

Instances persist until deleted and nothing times out mid-task. If the wallet goes negative and automatic top-up cannot charge, instances are suspended; an instance left suspended for 30 days is permanently deleted.
Backups, restore and fork are offered; we count these as snapshots. No GPU option is described.

bestFor: One persistent instance per end user or agent that sits idle most of the day, using auto-sleep to pay mostly for disk.
Hosting agent harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode as always-on instances.
Small, steady workloads on a prepaid balance with no plan fee.
watchOut: Default instances are gVisor containers on shared hosts; full VMs cost 2.5x compute.
Default instances stop at 4 vCPU / 32 GB; the 8 vCPU / 64 GB shape needs a VM or Performance instance, at 2.5x or 4x compute.
Default instances run only in the United States; other regions require VM instances.
Running instances at once are capped by total top-ups, starting at 3.

providers.name: Airtop
providers.tagline: Cloud browsers with natural-language controls and an agent builder, sold as monthly credit plans.
providers.summary: Airtop runs cloud browser sessions that agents control through its API with natural-language actions such as page queries and form filling, or directly with Puppeteer, Playwright or Selenium. It also sells Agent Builder, which compiles described workflows into scheduled agents, and Mark, a marketing assistant. All usage, including browser time, proxy bandwidth and AI calls, is paid in credits from a monthly plan, but Airtop does not publish how many credits a browser-hour uses. Plans run from a free tier with 1,000 credits a month to $558 a month.

providers.name: Alibaba Cloud Agent Sandbox
providers.tagline: E2B-compatible VM-isolated sandboxes for AI agents on Alibaba Cloud, billed per second with hibernation states.
providers.summary: Agent Sandbox is Alibaba Cloud's isolated execution environment for AI agents, with code, browser, desktop and mobile sandbox types. The fully managed Flash Edition works with the E2B SDK and CLI, while the Container Edition exposes sandboxes through the Kubernetes API on Container Compute Service. Each sandbox runs in its own VM environment, and a newer MicroVM runtime in beta adds snapshots, forking and Windows. Billing is per second for vCPU, memory and disk above a 15 GiB free allowance, in three compute classes; idle sandboxes can drop into light or deep hibernation, which stops CPU or CPU and memory charges.
providers.isolation: Each sandbox runs in an independent VM environment; the second-generation runtime (beta) uses lightweight MicroVM isolation
sdks: Java and Go SDKs maintained by Alibaba Cloud
providers.regions: Flash Edition: China (Beijing, Ulanqab, Shanghai, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong), Singapore, Malaysia (Johor), US (Virginia) and US (Silicon Valley). Container Edition: over 25 regions across China, Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Americas and the Middle East.

rates.billingIncrement: per second, 1-second minimum, billed hourly
rates.billedWhile: While active: vCPU, memory and disk above 15 GiB, on the size set at creation. Light hibernation (Flash Edition only): memory and disk, no vCPU. Deep hibernation and saved snapshots: storage only, for memory size plus disk size. Nothing after the sandbox is destroyed.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.limits: Three compute classes (Economy, Default, Performance) with the same billing rules and different unit prices. Flash Edition default quota of 300 sandboxes per region.

pricing.freeTier: No free trial or monthly allowance is stated for Agent Sandbox; only the first 15 GiB of disk on an active sandbox is free.
notes: Listed rates are the Default (recommended) class for China (Hong Kong) and regions outside China: USD 0.017856 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.008928 per GiB-hour of memory.

Outside mainland China, the Economy class is USD 0.013716 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.006876 per GiB-hour; the Performance class (Flash Edition only, dedicated resource pool) is USD 0.027324 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.013896 per GiB-hour.
Chinese mainland regions are cheaper: the Default class is USD 0.01224 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.006012 per GiB-hour.

Disk is USD 0.00025308 per GiB-hour outside mainland China; per 730-hour month that is about USD 0.1847 per GiB. An active sandbox gets 15 GiB free, but hibernated sandboxes and snapshots pay for all stored data, counted as memory size plus disk size.
Pre-warming custom templates is billed at the disk rate from November 15, 2026; official templates are not charged for pre-warming.
Other Alibaba Cloud services used alongside the sandbox, such as storage or internet egress, are billed by those services.
Pause and resume are available only to allowlisted accounts, and snapshots are an invited test that needs the second-generation runtime; snapshots expire after 7 days by default.
A sandbox can run at most 86,400 seconds (24 hours) at a time in the active state.
Maximum vCPU and memory per sandbox and GPU support for the managed Flash Edition are not stated on the pages checked.

The Flash Edition is closely tied to FC Agent Sandbox in Function Compute, whose documentation describes the same per-second model under Eco, Std and Pro plan names; the Java and Go SDKs are maintained by the Function Compute team.

bestFor: Teams already on Alibaba Cloud, or serving users in China and Asia-Pacific, that need agent sandboxes
Moving E2B SDK code to another provider by changing the endpoint and API key
Long agent sessions that wait on models or people, since hibernation stops CPU and memory charges
Reinforcement learning rollouts and evaluations that clone many sandboxes from one checkpoint

The MicroVM runtime that adds snapshots and Windows is still beta and only accepts Ubuntu- or Debian-based images

providers.name: Amp
providers.tagline: Coding agent that gives every thread its own cloud machine (an orb), with published per-size hourly prices.
providers.summary: Amp is a coding agent where each new thread can run in its own cloud machine, called an orb, with the repository cloned and tools installed. Orbs come in fixed sizes from 1 vCPU / 2 GB ($0.08/hour) to 16 vCPU / 44 GB, are billed by the minute while running, and pause automatically when idle with files and memory kept. The free Hobby tier pays the standard per-size price for hosted orbs; the $20 Megawatt and $200 Gigawatt tiers (and a $50 Megawatt 50 option offered after sign-in) include a monthly block of orb time, and self-hosted orbs or your own runners cost nothing on these tiers. Model usage is separate: bring your own subscription or API key, or buy credits at provider list price.
providers.isolation: Separate sandboxed cloud machine per thread; Amp's security page says e2b provides the compute instances. The isolation technology is not stated by Amp.
providers.regions: Not stated for orbs. Amp's main infrastructure is on Google Cloud in the US.

rates.billingIncrement: per minute
rates.billedWhile: Only while the orb is running. An orb pauses 5 minutes after the agent stops working or 20 minutes after your last interaction, whichever is later; a paused orb costs nothing.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.limits: No monthly fee and no included orb time: hosted orbs are pay-as-you-go at the standard per-size prices. Self-hosted orbs and your own runners are free and unlimited. Use your own model subscription or API keys, or buy credits.

plans.name: Megawatt (Individual)
plans.limits: 750 hours (45,000 minutes) of a1.small (2 vCPU / 4 GB) orbs a month; larger orbs use the hours faster. Also $20 of agent usage for Amp-served models and tools. Allowance resets monthly and does not roll over; after it runs out, buy credits or upgrade. a1.3xlarge is not available.

plans.name: Megawatt 50 (Individual)
plans.limits: 2.5 times Megawatt's included agent and orb usage, which works out to 1,875 hours of a1.small (2 vCPU / 4 GB) orbs and $50 of agent usage a month. Offered only after sign-in, on the pricing page or in billing settings; it is not listed in the public tier table.

plans.name: Gigawatt (Individual)
plans.limits: 1,000 hours of a1.xxlarge (16 vCPU / 32 GB) orbs a month; larger orbs use the allowance faster and smaller ones more slowly. Also $200 of agent usage for Amp-served models and tools. Allowance resets monthly and does not roll over; after it runs out, buy credits.

pricing.freeTier: No free hosted orb time. The Hobby tier itself is free, and self-hosted orbs or your own runners cost nothing on Hobby, Individual and Teams tiers, but Amp-hosted orbs are pay-as-you-go.
notes: The cloud machine is priced separately from the agent. Hosted orb sizes and standard prices: a1.tiny 1 vCPU / 2 GB $0.08/hour, a1.small 2 / 4 GB $0.17/hour, a1.medium 4 / 8 GB $0.33/hour, a1.large 8 / 16 GB $0.66/hour, a1.xxlarge 16 / 32 GB $1.32/hour, a1.3xlarge 16 / 44 GB $2.13/hour. Every size has a 60 GB disk.

The per-vCPU and per-GB rates we show come from Amp's published formula for the standard price (CPUs x $0.0504/hour + GB memory x $0.0162/hour, quoted for self-hosted orbs that match no size). It reproduces the hosted size prices to the cent, except a1.3xlarge, which Amp prices higher because of compute scarcity (the formula would give about $1.52/hour).
Ambiguity: Amp states memory in GB without saying GB or GiB; we use the GB rate as the GiB rate.

Paid-tier orb allowances are stated as hours of one size: 750 a1.small hours on Megawatt and 1,000 a1.xxlarge hours on Gigawatt. Larger orbs use the hours faster; the exact conversion between sizes is not stated on the pages checked. We convert them to vCPU-hours and GB-hours of the named size. At standard prices Megawatt's 750 a1.small hours are worth about $127.50 and Gigawatt's 1,000 a1.xxlarge hours about $1,320.
Paid tiers also include agent usage for Amp-served models and tools: $20 a month on Megawatt ($10 with the education discount) and $200 on Gigawatt. After that, credits are bought at list price.

Signed-in users can also choose Megawatt 50 at $50 a month, with 2.5 times Megawatt's included agent and orb usage. Amp keeps it out of the public tier table. The 1,875 a1.small hours and $50 of agent usage we show for it are our arithmetic: 2.5 times Megawatt's 750 hours and $20.

Model usage is billed separately from orbs: use a ChatGPT, Claude or other subscription or your own API keys with no Amp token fees, or buy Amp credits charged at provider API prices with no markup for individuals and non-enterprise workspaces. Purchased credits expire 12 months after purchase.

There is no fixed run-time limit: the pause timeouts are idle timeouts, and an orb keeps running while the agent has work. A paused orb keeps its filesystem and memory, encrypted at rest, until the thread is deleted.
Each user can start a burst of 20 metered orbs, then one new orb every five minutes; later starts wait instead of failing.

Students and teachers can get Megawatt for $10 a month. Team workspaces have no extra fee; Enterprise pricing is custom. Self-hosted orbs are free on Hobby, Individual and Teams; Enterprise workspaces pay the standard price for them.

bestFor: Running many agent tasks in parallel, each in its own paused-when-idle cloud machine.
Developers who want to use their own ChatGPT or Claude subscription or API keys for models.
Teams that want to run the same agent on their own machines at no extra cost.

providers.name: Anchor Browser
providers.tagline: Cloud Chromium for agents with managed logins, billed in credits: $0.05 per browser-hour plus $0.01 per browser.
providers.summary: Anchor Browser provides hosted Chromium sessions that agents drive over CDP, its SDKs or MCP, with managed authentication, proxies, captcha bypass and a built-in AI task agent. Usage is paid in credits worth $1 each: browser sessions you drive yourself cost $0.01 per browser created plus $0.05 per browser-hour, with proxy data and AI steps extra. Saved automation tasks are instead billed a flat 0.1 credits per successful run, or the infrastructure cost if higher. A free plan gives 5 credits every month.

providers.summary: Archil sells durable disks for AI workloads and runs compute next to them: persistent sandboxes and one-shot serverless tool calls. providers.name: AWS Nitro Sandboxes
providers.tagline: Hardware-isolated lightweight VMs on your own EC2 instances, one per EKS pod, ECS task or agent session.
providers.summary: Nitro Sandboxes is an EC2 feature that runs each workload in its own lightweight VM on the Nitro Hypervisor, next to a parent EC2 instance that lends it vCPUs and memory. On EKS a pod opts in with one line in its spec, and on ECS Managed Instances each task can run in its own sandbox; on plain EC2 you launch them yourself with Firecracker. Confidential mode hides sandbox memory from the parent instance and adds attestation that gates key release in AWS KMS, while direct mode trusts the parent. There is no extra charge: you pay for the EC2 instances (and any EKS Auto Mode or ECS Managed Instances fee).

notes: No per-sandbox rate exists. Cost depends on the EC2 instance type you choose and how many sandboxes you pack onto it, so no vCPU or memory rate is listed.
EKS Auto Mode and ECS Managed Instances charge their standard management fee on top of EC2 if you use them.

Density: up to 5 sandboxes per parent vCPU and at most 896 per instance. A sandbox can have at most as many vCPUs as its parent, so the largest size depends on the instance type; no fixed maximum vCPU or memory is published. Each sandbox needs at least 256 MiB of memory.
On instances with two threads per core, a core runs only one sandbox at a time, so usable compute is about half the advertised vCPUs. Graviton instances are not affected.
Sandboxes live as long as the parent instance and you keep them; no maximum session length is published.
GPU passthrough is unavailable; on GPU instance types a sandbox runs CPU workloads only.

providers.name: boxd
providers.tagline: Persistent KVM microVMs that fork, checkpoint and hibernate, billed on active vCPU, resident RAM and written disk.
providers.summary: boxd runs persistent Linux machines in microVMs on its own KVM-based VMM, hosted in Frankfurt and New York. Machines default to 2 vCPU, 8 GiB and a 100 GiB disk, can be forked while running, checkpointed and snapshotted, and hibernate after 4 hours without network traffic, keeping their processes. Billing is credit-based and metered per second on active vCPU, resident memory and disk written, not on provisioned size. New organizations get 30 in free credits when they add a payment method, and the platform can also be self-hosted, free up to 16 vCPUs.
providers.isolation: Dedicated microVM per machine on boxd's own Rust VMM built on KVM
providers.regions: Frankfurt (Germany) and New York; machines and data in Frankfurt stay in the EU.

rates.billingIncrement: Metered every second, settled every 15 minutes, no minimum charge per machine

notes: Currency: boxd bills an organization in euros or US dollars, chosen when it is created. The rates shown are boxd's own USD prices: $0.047 per active vCPU-hour, $0.014 per GiB-hour of resident RAM and $0.000096 per GiB-hour of disk written. The euro rates are EUR 0.039, EUR 0.012 and EUR 0.00008.
Disk storage converted per 730-hour month: $0.000096 x 730 = $0.07008 per GiB-month (EUR 0.0584), charged on space written, not the 100 GiB provisioned.

Only active vCPU is billed: a 2 vCPU machine busy 10% of an hour pays for 0.2 vCPU-hours. boxd quotes a default 2 vCPU / 8 GiB machine at about EUR 0.17 / USD 0.21 per hour fully busy, and about EUR 0.03 / USD 0.04 per hour at 0.2 vCPU active, 2 GiB held and 20 GiB written.

States: running pays vCPU, RAM and disk; standby (paused, memory kept warm, resumes in under 1 ms) pays RAM and disk; hibernated (memory written to disk, wakes in about 156 ms) pays disk only. A machine hibernates on its own after 4 hours with no network traffic by default.

Self-serve sizes per the FAQ are 1 vCPU / 4 GiB, 2 vCPU / 8 GiB and 4 vCPU / 16 GiB, with 8 vCPU / 32 GiB or larger by email; the pricing page lists pay-as-you-go machines up to 8 vCPU / 32 GiB. We show 8 vCPU / 32 GiB.
Scale (same rates, higher limits, bring your own cloud) and self-host licences are priced by contact. Self-hosting is free up to 16 vCPUs with no licence key.

providers.tagline: V8 isolates created at runtime from a Worker to run untrusted JavaScript or WebAssembly, billed on CPU time.
providers.summary: Dynamic Workers let a Cloudflare Worker load and run code supplied at runtime in a new V8 isolate, as a lightweight alternative to containers. The parent Worker decides which bindings the code receives and can block, filter or rewrite its outbound requests. Billing uses Workers Standard rates for requests and CPU milliseconds (including isolate startup), plus a charge per unique Dynamic Worker created each day. It runs JavaScript and WebAssembly only, with 128 MB of memory per isolate.

providers.tagline: Persistent microVM machines for autonomous coding agents, with credential-injecting gateways and per-run cost tracking.
providers.summary: Islo, from the team behind Incredibuild, runs coding agents on persistent Linux machines, each in its own microVM, with the repository, dependencies, browser and tools prepared in advance. Agents can be triggered from Slack, GitHub or Linear, and a gateway injects credentials and enforces allow or deny rules on outbound traffic. Sandboxes pause on idle or on a runtime cap, keep their files, and can resume on the next request. Plans cost $20 a month for one engineer with one concurrent workflow, or $200 a month for a team of 10 with 50 concurrent workflows and 10 times the usage, with unlimited machines on both; Islo does not publish per-hour compute prices or how much usage a plan includes.

providers.name: Kortix
providers.tagline: Source-available agent platform, also called Suna, running each session on its own microVM, billed per second.
providers.summary: Kortix CompanyOS, the agent project also known as Suna, runs custom agents for code, research, apps and business work from the web, desktop and mobile apps, a CLI, Slack or Microsoft Teams. Every session gets its own isolated cloud computer with a terminal, a browser, a desktop, Python and Node.js, and works on its own branch of the workspace repository; changes land through a change request a person approves. The computers run on Platinum, Kortix's own microVM sandbox cloud. Unlike most hosted coding agents, the machine has a published price: credits at $0.01 each pay for compute per second, $0.0324 per vCPU-hour and $0.0108 per GB of memory per hour, so the default 2 vCPU / 4 GB computer costs about $0.11 an hour. Models are paid separately, through your own provider key, a ChatGPT subscription or Kortix-managed models. The Free plan gives 500 credits a month on the first workspace; paid plans start at $50 a month for 5,000 credits.

Model usage is separate from the computer. With your own provider key, the first $1,000 a month is free and then 5% of the provider's price is paid from credits. A connected ChatGPT subscription uses no credits. Kortix-managed models cost the provider's base price plus a 5.5% platform fee.
Web searches, scraping and residential IP traffic through Kortix are also paid from credits.

Only /workspace and the session's branch, Drive files and messages are kept while a computer sleeps; the home directory, /tmp and installed packages can be gone when it wakes. Tools that must persist go into a sandbox template.

Sandbox templates set the image (a tagged image or a Dockerfile with a Debian-family base) and the size. Kortix's developer docs accept sizes up to 32 vCPU, 128 GiB memory and 500 GiB disk, but Platinum, the sandbox cloud the session computers run on, now states up to 16 vCPU, 32 GB RAM and 100 GB disk per sandbox, with larger shapes by arrangement. We list Platinum's limit as the largest computer. GPUs are not offered.

An egress policy can be written in the project config, but Kortix states it does not enforce it. Secrets can be held outside the computer and swapped in only on requests to listed web addresses, and connector logins never enter the computer.
Self-hosting runs the web app, API and database on your own server, but sessions still run on Platinum cloud computers that call back to it.
Enterprise adds single sign-on, directory sync, advanced roles, audit logs and VPC or on-prem deployment at custom pricing.
The control plane can be installed on your own server, but session computers still run on Platinum's cloud, so it is not listed as self-hosted.

bestFor: Teams that want agents for code and non-code work sharing one repo of agents, skills and memory.
Running many agent sessions in parallel, each on its own sleeping-when-idle cloud computer.
Buyers who want a published per-second machine price instead of an opaque usage allowance.
watchOut: The license is the Elastic License 2.0, which is source-available and forbids offering the software to others as a hosted service.
Built as a general company agent platform rather than a coding-only agent.
Session computers always run on Platinum's cloud, even on a self-hosted install.
Outbound network restrictions in the project config are not enforced.
Files outside /workspace and installed packages can be lost when a sleeping computer wakes.

providers.name: kosa8 Cloud
providers.tagline: Hosted microVM sandboxes from the kosa8 agent-security tool, with Cloud hours included in every paid plan.
providers.summary: kosa8 runs each agent in a microVM with its own kernel, either on your own Mac or Linux machines or on kosa8 Cloud, its hosted service, which runs in one US region (Ashburn, Virginia) today. Cloud sandboxes are created from Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Ruby or Java SDKs or a REST API. There is no free tier and no pay as you go: every account picks a plan, from $29 a month, before it uses kosa8 anywhere. Each plan includes a monthly allowance of Cloud sandbox-hours (100 on Solo up to 1,000 a person on Scale; one sandbox-hour is an hour of a 2 vCPU / 4 GB sandbox), nothing is billed on top except browser sandboxes ($0.12 per browser-hour), and new work stops at the plan's limits. Sleeping sandboxes use no hours.
providers.isolation: Hardware-virtualised microVM per sandbox with its own kernel (Cloud Hypervisor on KVM on Linux)
providers.regions: One region today: US East (us-ash1, Ashburn, Virginia). There is no EU region yet; data that must stay elsewhere can run on your own servers joined as hosts, or on kosa8 run on your own infrastructure. When kosa8's hosts are full, a plain sandbox may run on overflow capacity (Cloudflare Containers) at the same price.

pricing.freeTier: No free tier, credit, trial or pay as you go. Every account adds a card and picks a plan, from $29 a month, charged at checkout, before it uses kosa8 on any platform, including your own computer. notes: From 16 November 2026 kosa8 dropped its free tier and Cloud pay as you go. Accounts made before that date keep working until 1 December 2026; after that, until a plan is picked, new work is paused and running sandboxes sleep.

One sandbox-hour is an hour of a 2 vCPU / 4 GB Cloud sandbox. Other sizes count by vCPU: a 1 vCPU template sandbox uses half an hour per hour, a 16 vCPU / 32 GiB one uses 8. Hours reset each month and do not roll over; on Team and Scale they are per person and pooled.

Limits are hard: at a limit new work stops, with nothing billed on top. Add-on packs raise one limit: +100 sandbox-hours for $15 a month, or +10 sandboxes running at once for $49 a month. The Cloud plan limits apply from December 2026.

Sizes are 1 vCPU / 256 MiB (templates; node 384 MiB), then 2, 4, 8 or 16 vCPUs with 2 GiB of RAM per vCPU, any OCI image, and a disk of 8 to 200 GB. The largest size each plan can run goes from 2 vCPU / 4 GB on Solo to 16 vCPU / 32 GB on Scale.

Small sizes for fleets of mostly idle sandboxes, on every plan: 0.25 vCPU / 512 MiB (0.125 sandbox-hours an hour), 0.5 vCPU / 1 GiB (0.25) and 1 vCPU / 2 GiB (0.5). They reserve that share of a vCPU and burst to a whole one (two for the 1 vCPU size) while the host has idle CPU; bursts are not billed.

Browser sandboxes (headless Chromium driven over CDP) cost $0.12 per browser-hour, billed per second, and each browser-hour also uses 0.125 sandbox-hours. Solo runs 1 at once, Pro 3, Team 5, Scale 10.
Paying yearly costs ten months' price. Team and Scale are priced per person, from one person.
Bring-your-own hosts cost $0.20 per host-hour, with no compute charge. Fork limits, fork overage ($0.10 per fork-hour, only if turned on) and sandbox disk sizes apply to use on your own machines.
kosa8 Cloud has egress allow and deny lists per sandbox. The API key broker, undo and other security features are for your own machines and are still coming to Cloud.

providers.name: Koyeb Sandboxes
providers.tagline: MicroVM sandboxes on Koyeb's serverless platform, billed per second at Koyeb instance prices, with CPU or GPU.
providers.summary: Koyeb Sandboxes are ephemeral environments created from Docker images with Koyeb's Python and JavaScript SDKs, running on the same microVM instances as Koyeb services. Each sandbox is billed per second at the price of its instance type, from $0.0036 per hour for 0.25 vCPU / 256 MB up to GPU instances such as an H100 at $2.50 per hour. Sandboxes scale to zero after an idle timeout and can be auto-deleted after up to 24 hours, and filesystem or full snapshots can seed new sandboxes. Sandboxes are in public preview and need a Starter (pay-as-you-go), Pro or Scale plan.

Smaller sizes are cheaper: nano 0.25 vCPU / 256 MB $0.0036, micro 0.5 vCPU / 512 MB $0.0072 (the SDK default).

Snapshots can be filesystem-only or full and are used to create new sandboxes. Outbound traffic can be blocked or limited to an IP/CIDR allowlist.

providers.name: Kubernetes Agent Sandbox
providers.tagline: Kubernetes controller for stateful agent sandboxes with warm pools; offered on GKE at no extra charge.
providers.summary: Agent Sandbox is a Kubernetes SIG Apps project that adds a Sandbox custom resource and controller for long-running, stateful single-pod workloads with a stable identity and persistent storage. Extensions add templates, claims and pre-warmed pools for fast allocation, plus Go and Python SDKs and an optional router. It orchestrates pods and leaves kernel isolation to a runtime class such as gVisor or Kata Containers. Google offers it on GKE at no extra charge beyond normal GKE resource pricing.

notes: Isolation strength depends on the runtime class you configure. Google's GKE docs warn that without gVisor or microVMs the pods run without kernel isolation and should not run untrusted code.
On GKE, Pod Snapshots can suspend idle sandboxes and resume them; that is a GKE feature, not part of the open-source controller.
GKE docs list GPUs and TPUs as a reason to choose Agent Sandbox; any pod resource your cluster supports can be requested.

Modal prices CPU per physical core, and one core equals 2 vCPU. Our vCPU-hour figure is the core rate divided by 2 ($0.141912 / 2 = $0.070956).

Billing is max(request, actual) for CPU and memory, with a minimum of 0.125 cores and 128 MiB per container. With no request set, a sandbox pays roughly for its average usage; a request is billed for the sandbox's whole lifetime even if idle. Disk requests add to the memory request at a 20:1 ratio.
GPU sandboxes are billed at the standard GPU rates listed above (per-second rates x3600), only run on the gVisor runtime, and are subject to preemption.
Pinning a region multiplies the price by 1.15x (broad region such as us) or 1.75x (narrow region such as us-west).

Sandbox timeout defaults to 5 minutes and can be set up to 24 hours; there is no pause/resume, but filesystem snapshots (30-day default TTL) and memory snapshots (alpha, 7-day expiry, terminates the sandbox) can carry state to a new sandbox.

Snapshot storage: 5 TB snapshot-hours per MCU = $0.05 / 5,000 GB-hours = $0.00001 per GB-hour = $0.0073 per GB-month at 730 hours. This matches the vendor example: an 8 vCPU / 8 GB RAM / 8 GB disk snapshot costs $0.12/month (16 GB snapshot).

Paid tiers are discounted MCU bundles: Team $40 for 1,000 MCUs (20% discount), Scale $250 for 7,500 MCUs (33% discount). providers.name: Render Sandboxes
providers.tagline: Firecracker microVMs on Render that suspend when idle, billed for active CPU time plus provisioned memory.
providers.summary: Render Sandboxes run each sandbox in its own Firecracker microVM, created and driven from the Render CLI, the TypeScript or Python SDK, or the API. CPU is billed at $0.12 per active CPU hour and memory at a fixed hourly rate for the compute plan's RAM while the sandbox runs; a suspended sandbox has no compute charge. By default a sandbox suspends after 15 minutes without commands or file transfers and resumes on the next one, and both the idle and runtime timeouts can be turned off so a sandbox runs indefinitely. The product is in public beta and runs in one region (Oregon).

providers.summary: Sailboxes are isolated Linux VMs from Sail Research, the inference provider, built for agents that run for hours or days. There is no runtime limit: a Sailbox can sleep or pause with memory and running processes saved, and checkpoints can start new Sailboxes from the same state. Billing follows actual use rather than reserved size: CPU time, physical RAM held and disk used are metered while the Sailbox runs, up to 64 vCPUs and 256 GiB per box. The free plan gives $5 of credit a month once a payment method is attached; Pro costs $250 a month with $100 of included credit.

providers.name: Solo Enterprise for Agent Substrate
providers.tagline: Supported Agent Substrate on your Kubernetes: each agent session in a gVisor or microVM sandbox, suspended when idle.
providers.summary: Solo.io's enterprise release of Agent Substrate and kagent, generally available since November 2026, runs AI agents on a Kubernetes cluster you operate. Agent Substrate is an open-source runtime, co-maintained by Solo.io and Google, that runs every agent session as an actor in its own gVisor or microVM sandbox on a pool of pre-started worker pods. When a turn ends it snapshots the actor's files and memory to object storage and frees the worker, then restores the actor on any free worker when the next request arrives. kagent adds declarative agents, harnesses for Claude Code, Codex and custom images, short-lived standalone sandboxes for scripts, and an egress gateway that injects credentials so the sandbox holds none. The enterprise build adds single sign-on, access control, tracing, air-gapped installs and support; it needs license keys and is priced by quote.
providers.isolation: gVisor sandbox per actor by default, or a microVM under Cloud Hypervisor with a Kata Containers kernel; many sandboxed actors share one worker pod, and plain containers are not supported
providers.regions: Any Kubernetes cluster you run: 1.34 or later in certificate compatibility mode, 1.37 or later in the default mode, including OpenShift. Air-gapped installs are supported.

rates.billingIncrement: Not applicable: enterprise license by quote; no usage rates are published
rates.billedWhile: Not applicable: software runs on your own cluster, and you pay your provider for its nodes and storage

pricing.freeTier: The open-source kagent and Agent Substrate projects are free to run yourself. The enterprise release, with support, single sign-on, access control, tracing and air-gapped installs, needs license keys priced by quote from Solo.io sales.
notes: No public prices. Solo.io says enterprise pricing depends on scope, environments and support needs.
The enterprise install needs two license keys: one for kagent and one for agentgateway, which runs the router and egress gateway in front of the sandboxes.
Each worker can hold up to 1,000 actors. Each agent actor defaults to a limit of 1 CPU and 1 GiB of memory, which the operator can change; no upper size limit is published.
Standalone sandboxes expire after a set lifetime of at most 24 hours, counted from creation. Agent conversations instead suspend between turns and are cleaned up after seven idle days by default.
A default install requests 2.92 vCPU and 5.25 GiB for the control components before any agent runs. You also provide PostgreSQL for production.

Compute ($0.0504 per vCPU-hour) and allocated memory ($0.0162 per GiB-hour) bill per second while a sandbox is active; pausing checkpoints memory, processes and files and stops compute billing, and storage bills for retained data. providers.name: Vercel Sandbox
providers.tagline: Firecracker microVMs on Vercel, billed for active CPU time plus provisioned memory.
providers.summary: Vercel Sandbox runs each session in a Firecracker microVM, created from the JavaScript/TypeScript or Python SDK or the sandbox CLI. CPU is billed only for time the code actively uses it, while memory is billed for the full provisioned amount for as long as the session runs (2 GB per vCPU). Sandboxes are persistent by default: stopping one snapshots its filesystem (billed as snapshot storage) and the next call resumes it in a new session of up to 24 hours on Pro. Hobby includes a monthly usage allowance at no cost; Pro usage draws from the plan's $20 monthly credit.

Sandbox creations cost $0.60 per million. Data transfer (outbound plus all exposed-port traffic) is included in the Flat Rate CDN on Pro and $0.15/GB on Enterprise; downloads into the sandbox are free.
